title: Bound one triangular parity-split prefix by 3/2 (no new κ)
body:
## Summary

One parity split of the triangular Toeplitz compiler has infinity norm at most `3/2` when the off-diagonal coefficient `l1` is at most `1/2`. This is the prefix-norm step left open by `research/one-factor-of-t`. It branches from fetched main and does not replay that package.

Let `T` be lower triangular Toeplitz with constant term `1` and tail `l1` at most `η ≤ 1/2`. Write the symbol as `e(z^2) + z o(z^2)`, and let `a` and `b` be the coefficient `l1` norms of `e − 1` and of `o`. Then `a + b ≤ η`. The Neumann bound `‖e^{−1}‖_1 ≤ 1/(1 − a)` and the shared budget give:

- the even child satisfies `‖E − I‖_∞ ≤ a ≤ η`;
- `k = o/e` satisfies `‖k‖_1 ≤ b/(1 − a) ≤ η`, so each shear has infinity norm at most `1 + η`;
- the Schur child satisfies `‖S − I‖_∞ ≤ a + b ≤ η`.

At `η = 1/2` every factor is at most `3/2`. That is sharper than the descendant cap `η/(1 − η) = 1` in `SHALLOW-TOEPLITZ.md`. The pure odd symbol `(1, 1/2, 0, 0)` meets `3/2` on the completed map and on the right-shear prefix. The three-factor product identity holds in integers over denominator `4`. Replacing that coefficient `1/2` by `1` makes the tail `l1` equal to `1` and raises the same prefix from `3/2` to `2`. A perturbation of total `l1` at most `ε` keeps the `3/2` cap only when `η + ε ≤ 1/2`.

This is one prefix. It does not prove a second nested split, the `O(log^2 N)` compiler, the generator-shear compiler, the completed Gaussian stage, or that the dyadic `p^100` normalizer absorbs the prefix. No new κ. The selected record is `60403/20000000`.

## Test plan

- [x] `python3.12 -B scripts/research_package.py --package research/triangular-parity-prefix`
- [x] Prints `PASS_TRIANGULAR_PARITY_PREFIX` and `outcome=completed`
- [ ] Maintainer replay was not run
